title: Response Consistency SLA and Customer Migration Playbook
author: Priya Kapoor
content:
Summary:
This document defines the Response Consistency SLA framework (RCSLA), the policy and technical controls we will expose to customers to guarantee deterministic response characteristics, and a step-by-step migration playbook for moving customers from existing fidelity/packaging models to RCSLA-backed offerings. It combines product requirements, operational runbook tasks, pricing guidance, and customer communications designed for a staged rollout across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Goals:
- Provide clear, measurable guarantees for response consistency (latency stability, token fidelity, and determinism).
- Minimize customer disruption when migrating to the RCSLA model.
- Align pricing and billing incentives to operational cost while preserving quality.
- Create repeatable testing and validation steps so that SRE, Support, and Solutions teams can certify migrations.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: Redwood-hosted API, Redwood Dedicated, and Redwood Private (VPC) deployments.
- Audience: Product managers, SRE, Solutions Engineering, Customer Success, Sales, and Engineering teams executing migrations.

Background and motivation:
Historically, customers chose among fidelity packages that traded cost for output variability. As customers scale, product owners require contractual guarantees about response behavior (e.g., p95 latency windows, determinism for idem-potent pipelines, bounded quality drift for quantization rolls). RCSLA formalizes these guarantees into: a) measurable SLOs, b) operator-visible controls (batching, cache pinning, kernel selection), and c) migration patterns with minimal risk.

Terminology (short):
- Response Consistency: Combined property of latency stability, repeatability (determinism for same prompt + seed), and fidelity (no regression beyond defined thresholds).
- Determinism: Same input and model variant produce identical token sequence every run (when enabled).
- Fidelity Budget: Numeric allowance for acceptable delta in evaluation metrics (e.g., exact-match, ROUGE-L) when applying performance/quantization changes.
- RCSLA Tier: One of Platinum / Gold / Standard that maps to specific SLOs and billing terms.

RCSLA Tiers (summary):
We will expose three primary Response Consistency tiers. Each tier defines: latency window (p95), determinism guarantee, fidelity budget, and operational commitments (planned maintenance windows, rollback SLAs).

ASCII table:
Tier | p95 latency (tokens=128) | Determinism | Fidelity budget (eval delta) | Planned maintenance notice
-----|-------------------------|-------------|----------------------------|--------------------------
Platinum | <= 75 ms | optional determinism opt-in, 99.99% | max -0.3% EM / -0.6 ROUGE-L | 72 hours notice + can request blackout
Gold     | <= 150 ms | probabilistic stable outputs (99.5% token-match) | max -1.0% EM / -1.2 ROUGE-L | 48 hours notice
Standard | <= 300 ms | no determinism guarantee | max -3.0% EM / -3.5 ROUGE-L | 24 hours notice

SLOs and thresholds (service-level specifics):
- Latency: p95 measured at Redwood edge for standard request shape (prompt=80 tokens, gen=128 tokens). Use the Redwood Console metric path: metrics.request.latency.p95 per-tenant per-route. SLO burn is tracked hourly.
- Error budget: 0.1% monthly for Platinum, 0.5% monthly for Gold, 1% monthly for Standard. Error budget sources include server errors (5xx), timeout, and degraded fidelity rollbacks.
- Fidelity regression guard: Any model release that increases regression beyond tier's fidelity budget triggers automatic canary rollback by the runtime.

Service controls exposed to customers:
- determinism=true|false (API flag) — available on Platinum only; under the hood this sets RNG seeding and disables nondeterministic kernels.
- consistency_hint: {low, medium, high} — used by automatic batching and kernel selection to trade cost vs. stability.
- fidelity_tolerance: numeric percentage for custom fidelity governance at tenant level (Gold+).
Example API snippet (JSON):
{
  "model": "rwd-neo-XXL-v2",
  "prompt": "<customer prompt>",
  "determinism": true,
  "consistency_hint": "high",
  "max_tokens": 128
}

Migration playbook (high level, repeatable for each customer):
Pre-migration planning (Solutions Eng + Customer Success):
1) Gather telemetry: collect 14-day baseline for latency distribution, token costs, and quality metrics using customer-provided prompt-set (min 200 examples). Use Redwood Optimize instrumentation to produce baseline report.
2) Tier recommendation: propose RCSLA tier aligned to customer's SLO needs and economics (include cost delta and expected token savings).
3) Contract changes: attach RCSLA addendum to customer contract (legal to approve blackout terms).
4) Migration window: agree on target window and rollback criteria.

Migration execution (SRE + Runtime + Solutions):
1) Canary stage (3–7 days): enable deterministic mode for 1% of traffic (Platinum candidates) or high consistency_hint for Gold trials. Monitor: latency.p95, fidelity metrics, customer-observed deltas.
2) Validation gates: after 72 hours, pass if: latency within tier target, fidelity regression <= budget, error rate within error budget.
3) Broad rollout: increment to 10%, 25%, 50%, 100% in 24–72 hour increments depending on telemetry stability. Each step requires automated gate checks.
4) Post-rollout watch: 14-day high-sensitivity monitoring window where SRE and Solutions actively monitor dashboards and remain on-call for escalations.

Rollback procedure (automated + manual):
- Automatic rollback: runtime triggers if fidelity regression > 2x budget OR error budget consumed > 50% in an hour.
- Manual rollback: Solutions Eng can trigger tenant-level rollback via Admin Console: set determinism=false and revert model variant to the pinned version. CLI example: rwd-admin rollback --tenant <id> --reason "fidelity-exceed"

Testing & validation checklist (before signoff):
- Unit tests for determinism toggle (seeded repeat runs produce identical token streams).
- Integration test: full request path (ingress -> runtime -> telemetry -> console) with synthetic load for 200rps sustained.
- Eval harness: run customer prompt-set on control and candidate stacks and compute the exact-match and ROUGE-L deltas.
- End-to-end customer verification: Solutions Eng coordinates an acceptance test suite with the customer; acceptance requires <=tier fidelity delta and p95 target.

Billing and pricing impact:
- Pricing model: RCSLA is a premium add-on with a per-token uplift and commitment discount tiered by Platinum/Gold/Standard.
- Chargeable items: determinism opt-in (flat monthly surcharge for instance isolation), consistency compute premium (per-token %), and dedicated SLO credit for Platinum (annual subscription).
- Example pricing matrix (illustrative):
Tier | base token uplift | determinism surcharge | typical uplift range
Platinum | +25% | +$2,500/month | +30–45% total
Gold     | +12% | n/a | +12–18% total
Standard | +0%  | n/a | baseline pricing
- Billing events: when a tenant is rolled to a higher tier mid-billing-cycle, prorated charges are applied and visible in the Console billing preview. Finance to confirm in billing-ops runbook.

Operational runbook (SRE focus):
- Dashboards to create: per-tenant RCSLA overview (latency p50/p95, fidelity delta, error budget remaining), aggregated tier health, canary watchlist.
- Alerts:
  - RCSLA.Platinum.LatencySpike when p95 > 90ms for 10m (severity P2).
  - RCSLA.Fidelity.Alert when canary fidelity delta exceeds budget for two consecutive 10m windows (severity P1).
  - RCSLA.Rollback.Executed when runtime triggers an automated rollback (inform on-call and Solutions Eng).
- On-call play: initial responder reinspects canary nodes, verifies kernel selection logs and quantization flags, escalates to runtime team if rollback triggered.

Customer communication templates (brief):
- Pre-migration notice: 72-hr email that summarizes expected behavior, blackout windows, rollback plan, and contact details.
- Post-migration status: 14-day summary with measured deltas and cost impact.
(Templates appended as Appendix A).

Rollout schedule (recommended):
Phase 0 (Nov 2029): internal pilot with 3 internal customers (Dedicated + Hosted).
Phase 1 (Dec 2029 - Jan 2030): invite-only customers (PLG enterprise pilots) — limit 10 customers.
Phase 2 (Feb 2030 - Apr 2030): general availability for new customers; migration paths open for existing customers via Solutions Eng engagements.

Success metrics and KPIs:
- Adoption: % of top 50 customers enrolled in RCSLA within 6 months. Target 40%.
- Quality: aggregate fidelity regression < 0.6% across all migrations.
- Economics: realized per-token cost delta improvement of >= 10% for customers that applied recommended consistency_hint changes.
- Reliability: automated rollback rate < 2% of migrations.

Appendices:
A) Email templates (short):
- Pre-migration subject: "[Redwood] Upcoming migration: Response Consistency SLA trial for <tenant>"
  Body: Hi <contact>, we plan to enable the RCSLA <tier> for your tenant on <date>. Expected impact: p95 -> <target>, determinism: <on/off>. See migration plan attached.

B) CLI commands and admin checklist:
- Generate baseline report: rwd-cli optimize baseline --tenant <id> --prompt-set prompts.json --out baseline-report.json
- Enable determinism (admin): rwd-admin set-tenant-flag --tenant <id> --flag determinism=true --actor <owner>
- Rollback tenant: rwd-admin rollback --tenant <id> --reason "fidelity-exceed"

C) Evaluation metrics to capture: exact_match, rouge_l, perplexity_delta, token_cost_usd, p95_latency_ms.
